full_judgment:
2. These two appeals by special leave are against the judgment and order dated the 28th day of August, 2008 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos.4678 and 4679 of 2008 making the Rules absolute. 

 3. Facts giving rise to these appeals are that Md. Idris Ali, Sub-Inspector of RAB-1, Uttara, Dhaka lodged a First Information Report (FIR) with Gulshan Police Station on 26.10.2007 at about 20:05 hours alleging, inter-alia, that he along with a contingent of high powered RAB-1 officials having received information, that there were a lot of Yaba tablets, phensydils, foreign liquors, Ice pill tablets and machineries for manufacturing Yaba tablets at House No.41, Road No.123 under Gulshan Police Station, raided the said house on 25.10.2007 at 00:05 hours and recovered 132 bottles of phensydils, Viagra tablet and some foreign currencies. On the basis of the said FIR, Gulshan Police Station Case No,61 dated 26.10.2007 was started against the respondent and another under section 25(B)(2) of the Special Power Act, 1974. Another FIR was lodged by Sub-Inspector Mohammad Nurul Alam of RAB-1, Uttara, Dhaka with Gulshan Police Station on the same day making similar allegations, the place of recovery of the incriminating materials being House No.43, 3, CE/S/A, Gulshan-1, at Road No.116 and on the basis of the said FIR Gulshan Police Station Case No.62 dated 26.10.2007 under table 9(kha) of section 19(1)/20/22(ga) of the Narcotics Control Act, 1990 (the Act, 1990) was started against the respondent and another. 

 4. Police after investigation submitted charge-sheets in both the cases against the appellant and another on 27.11.2007 under item Nos.5 and 9(kha) of the Table to section 19(1) and item Nos.5 and 9 (kha) of the Table to section 19 (1) /20 /22(ga) of the Act, 1990 respectively. After submission of charge-sheets, the case records were transmitted to the Druta Bichar Tribunal No.4, Dhaka where the cases were registered as Druta Bichar Tribunal Case Nos.4 of 2008 and 13 of 2008. The Tribunal by its order dated 31.01.2008 framed charges in both the cases against the accused-respondent and the co-accused under table 5 and 9(kha) of section 19(1) of the Act, 1990. 

 5. At this stage of the cases, the respondent filed two applications before the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the proceedings of the said two Druta Bichar Tribunal cases. In both the applications, Rules were issued by the High Court Division giving rise to Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos.4678 and 4679 of 2008. At the time of issuance of the Rules, further proceedings of both the Druta Bichar Tribunal cases were stayed. 

 6. A Division Bench of the High Court Division after hearing the criminal miscellaneous cases by the judgment and order dated 28.08.2008 made the Rules absolute and quashed the proceedings of the said two Druta Bichar Tribunal cases. Against the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the State filed Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal. Nos.594 of 2008 and 595 of 2008 and leave was granted by this Court to consider the submissions made by the learned Deputy Attorney General to the effect: 

 (a) the Government being empowered by law by Notification in the official Gazette having appointed an inspector of RAB-1, Uttara, Dhaka to investigate the case there was no illegality in the process of investigation of the case, the High Court Division erred in law in quashing the proceedings; 

 10. In view of the leave granting order and the submission made by the learned Counsel for the respondent, the moot question to be decided in these two appeals is whether the High Court Division correctly interpreted section 39 of the Act, 1990 in quashing the druta bichar tribunal cases in question on the applications filed by the respondent under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (the Code). 

 12. We have gone through the various provisions of the Act, 1990. In the Act, no specific provision has been made as to the lodging of an FIR in respect of an offence committed thereunder, its investigation as well as trial, in case charge-sheet is submitted after investigation. So, we are also to see, in the absence of any provision in the Act, 1990, how an FIR shall he lodged in respect of an offence committed thereunder and then its investigation shall be conducted and its trial be held. But at the outset, we want to consider section 39 of the Act, 1990, which runs thus: 

 13. A reading of section 39 of the Act, 1990 as quoted herein before shows that sub-section (1) has given the power of an officer-in-charge of a police station to the Director General of the Narcotics Directorate to investigate into an offence committed under the Act. Sub-section (2) of the said section shows that the Government may also confer power of an officer-in- charge of a police station to an officer subordinate to the Director General by a gazette notification to investigate into an offence committed under the Act, 1990. The very language of section 39 of the Act, 1990 shows that the power of the Director General of the Directorate of Narcotics to investigate into an offence committed thereunder is not in derogation of the power of an officer-in-charge of the concerned police station given under the provisions of the Code to investigate into an offence committed under the Act. The language of the section which is clear and unambiguous does not show that it is only the Director General of the Directorate of  Narcotics or any other officer subordinate to him specially empowered by the Government by a gazette notification who shall have the exclusive and absolute power to investigate into an offence committed under the Act, 1990. In this regard, it is very pertinent to state that section 31 of the Act, 1990 has made the offences committed under the Act cognizable and, therefore, the power of the officer-in-charge of the concerned police station or ally other police officer of the police station to whom endorsement may be made by the officer-in-charge to investigate the case under the Code cannot be curtailed or taken away. Moreover, in the Act, 1990, here being no specific provision as to the lodging of an FIR and its investigation as of necessity, the provisions of the Code would automatically come into play in respect of the above matter in view of the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 5 of the Code. Sub-section (2) of section 5 of the Code has clearly mandated that all offences under any other law shall be investigated, inquired into, tried, and otherwise dealt with according to the same provisions, but subject to any enactment for the time being in force regulating the manner or place of investigating, inquiring into, trying or otherwise dealing with such offences. And, in fact, the respective FIR's giving rise to the druta bichar cases in question were lodged under section 154 of the Code as is apparent from the very first page of the respective FIR's. 

 15. A reading of section 44 shows that on a written request made by the Director General of the Directorate of Narcotics the investigating authority may hand over the charge of investigation of a case to an officer specified by him and that officer shall have the authority to investigate the case either from the beginning or the stage from which he was given the charge of investigation. Thus, section 44 of the Act, 1990 prima-facie, shows that besides the Director General of the Directorate of Narcotics, or an officer subordinate to him specially empowered by the Government by gazette notification, investigation of an offence committed under the Act shall also be done by other agency and that agency cannot but be an agency as contemplated in the Code in view of sub-section (2) of section 5 thereof. Had the Director General of Narcotics Directorate or any officer subordinate to him specially empowered by the Government by the gazette notification the exclusive authority to investigate into an offence committed under the Act, 1990, than the question of making request by the Director General to hand over charge of investigation of a case to an officer specified by him as provided in section 44 of the Act would not have arisen. But the learned Judges of the high Court Division failed to consider the provision of sub-section (2) of section 5 of the Code as well as section 44 of the Act, 1990 in interpreting section 39 thereof. In the context, the learned Judges of the high Court Division also misread the plain and unambiguous language of section 39 of the Act, 1990 in holding that the section has made it mandatory to investigate an offence committed under the Act either by the Director General, Directorate of 6. Narcotics or an officer subordinate to him as provided in sub-section (2) thereof. The learned Judges also failed to consider that the Government has the power to appoint a police officer, or a member of any other law enforcing agency otherwise competent under the law to investigate a case. In the instant case, since the respective FIR's were lodged with Gulshan Police Station, the Government appointed an officer of RAB-1, Uttara to investigate the cases and in doing so no wrong was committed by it, so we do not see any lack of jurisdiction on the part of the said officer of RAB to investigate the case and on completion of investigation to submit the charge sheets, therefore, the question of vitiating the entire "proceeding" of investigation of the case "and thereafter" as found by the High Court Division does not arise at all. 

 16. In view of the discussions made hereinbefore, we do not consider it at all necessary to dwell upon the meaning of the word 'subordinate' as dealt with by the High Court Division and also to consider the cases referred to in the impugned judgment. 

 17. For the discussions made above, we hold that the High Court Division totally misread, misconceived and misinterpreted the provisions of section 39 of the Act, 1990 and thus, fell into an error in quashing the impugned proceedings on the erroneous view that the investigation of the case having been conducted by an officer of RAB the whole "proceeding" of investigation as well as the proceedings thereafter were vitiated. 

 18. In the result, the appeals are allowed, the trial Court is directed to proceed with the cases as usual.
